title: Financial Irregularities in Cooperative Societies
body_text:
As per the National Cooperative Database (NCD), out of a total 8.53 lakh Cooperative Societies across the country, 6.63 lakh are functional, 1.41 lakh are non-functional and 49,177 are under liquidation. Among 6.63 lakh functional cooperative societies, 5.95 lakh societies are audited and 0.68 lakh societies are not audited. The State-wise details of functional and audited cooperatives societies are attached as Annexure-1 . The details of cooperative societies lying dormant due to financial irregularities, weak management and lack of timely audits is maintained by respective State / UTs.
Further, Cooperative Societies registered under the provisions of the Multi-State Cooperative Societies (MSCS) Act, 2002 function as autonomous cooperative organisations and accountable to their members. In case of irregularities including financial embezzlement, winding up proceeding u/s 86 of the MSCS Act, 2002 are initiated against such MSCSs and liquidator is appointed under the provisions of Section 89 of MSCS Act, 2002 to liquidate the assets of Society and to ensure payment to investors/members under the provisions of section 90 of the Act. So far, 115 Multi-State Cooperative Societies are put under liquidation. The State-wise number of such societies is attached as Annexure-2 .
The Ministry of Cooperation, since its inception on 06.07.2021, has undertaken several initiatives to ensure transparency, accountability and protection of members' interests in cooperative societies under the vision of "Sahakar-se-Samriddhi."  Key initiatives include:
The Multi-State Cooperative Societies (MSCS) Act, 2002 was amended in 2023 to strengthen governance, enhance transparency, increase accountability and reform electoral process, etc. in the Multi State Cooperative Societies (MSCS). A Cooperative Rehabilitation, Reconstruction and Development Fund was established under section 63A of the Multi-State Cooperative Societies (MSCS) (Amendment) Act, 2023 to revive sick Multi-State Cooperative Societies and provide financial assistance for meeting their infrastructure requirements. Circulation of Model Byelaws of PACS, enabling diversification of activities such as storage, processing, LPG distribution, and common service centers, ensuring better governance standards and promoting member-centric operations. Strengthening of PACS through Computerization of PACS project by bringing functional PACS onto a common ERP-based national software, thereby improving transparency, efficiency, record management and service delivery. Capacity building and skill development programmes through National Council for Co-operative Training (NCCT) for members, Board of Directors, employees of cooperative, state officials and aspiring youth across the country with a network of 20 training institutes. Development of the National Cooperative Database (NCD) which serves as a comprehensive digital repository of 8.53 lakh cooperative societies across the country, having approximately 32 crore members. Inclusion of Rural Cooperative Banks under the RBI Integrated Ombudsman Scheme to bring greater transparency and accountability.

enrichment.summary: In a Lok Sabha written reply, the Ministry of Cooperation shared National Cooperative Database (NCD) data showing 8.53 lakh cooperative societies in India, of which 6.63 lakh are functional, 1.41 lakh non-functional, and 49,177 under liquidation; of the functional ones, 5.95 lakh are audited and 68,020 are not. Separately, 115 Multi-State Cooperative Societies (MSCS) are under liquidation under the MSCS Act, 2002, with Rajasthan (26) and Maharashtra (23) having the highest numbers. The Ministry listed reforms since its 2021 inception—including the 2023 MSCS Act amendment, a Cooperative Rehabilitation Fund, PACS computerization, Model Byelaws, and inclusion of rural cooperative banks under RBI's Ombudsman Scheme—aimed at improving transparency and accountability in the sector.
enrichment.context:
The Ministry of Cooperation was carved out as a separate ministry in July 2021 (previously cooperation was under the Ministry of Agriculture) to give the cooperative movement, comprising nearly 8.5 lakh societies and about 32 crore members, dedicated policy attention under the 'Sahakar-se-Samriddhi' vision. Cooperatives are a state subject under the Constitution, but Multi-State Cooperative Societies (MSCS), which operate across state boundaries, fall under central jurisdiction via the MSCS Act, 2002. The 97th Constitutional Amendment (2011) had earlier introduced Article 43B and Part IXB to promote autonomous, democratic, and professionally managed cooperatives, but implementation gaps, financial irregularities, and weak audits persisted, prompting reforms.

The 2023 amendment to the MSCS Act strengthened governance and electoral processes for MSCS, partly in response to scams and mismanagement in entities like credit cooperatives, and created a Cooperative Rehabilitation, Reconstruction and Development Fund to revive financially sick MSCS. Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS), the grassroots rural credit institutions, are being computerized and diversified (e.g., into LPG distribution, storage, common service centres) to make them financially viable and multi-functional, reducing rural dependence on informal credit. The National Cooperative Database and inclusion of rural cooperative banks under the RBI Integrated Ombudsman Scheme reflect a broader push toward digital transparency and grievance redressal in a sector historically prone to weak audits and financial embezzlement, as underscored by the significant number of non-audited societies and MSCS under liquidation cited in this release.

prelims_questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Multi-State Cooperative Societies (MSCS) in India:
1. MSCS are registered and regulated under the Multi-State Cooperative Societies Act, 2002.
2. Winding up of an MSCS due to financial irregularities is initiated under Section 86 of the MSCS Act, 2002.
3. The Cooperative Rehabilitation, Reconstruction and Development Fund was established through the 97th Constitutional Amendment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: MSCS are governed by the MSCS Act, 2002, and Section 86 deals with winding up proceedings for irregularities. The Cooperative Rehabilitation Fund was established under Section 63A of the MSCS (Amendment) Act, 2023, not the 97th Constitutional Amendment, making statement 3 incorrect.

prelims_questions.question: The Ministry of Cooperation in India was created in which year, and which body maintains the National Cooperative Database referred to for cooperative society statistics?
prelims_questions.explanation: The Ministry of Cooperation was established on 06.07.2021, and it maintains the National Cooperative Database (NCD) as a digital repository of cooperative society data across India.
